blurb:
Laredos is our go-to when we want Mexican without overthinking it. Colorful, loud in a fun way, and the kind of spot where you show up hungry and leave happy. Good for a weeknight dinner with the family or a casual outing when someone wants a margarita and chips before they've even looked at the menu.

The Mexican classics are what people come for, and the margaritas have a solid following. Nothing fussy about this place, and that's exactly the point.

They're open seven days a week, which is more than most spots around here can say. Easy to fit into any schedule.

blurb:
Lemon Grass on Roswell Road is where my wife and I land when we want Thai done right without any surprises. Big dining room, red decor, calm vibe. Good for a date night or a quiet weeknight dinner when you don't want anything too loud or chaotic.

The noodle dishes and curries are what people keep coming back for. Both solid. If you've never been, start with one of each and see what clicks for you.

One thing worth knowing: they close between lunch and dinner. Lunch service runs until 2:30pm and dinner doesn't start again until 5 or 5:30 depending on the day. Don't show up at 3:30 expecting to get seated. Also closed Sundays.

blurb:
Turmeric is one of those places I tell people about when they say they haven't found a good Indian spot in Marietta yet. It's on Sandy Plains, easy to get to, and the food is consistently good across the board. High rating, tons of reviews, and the kind of place where the lunch specials alone are worth the trip.

Reviewers rave about the lunch specials specifically, and I get it. Great value, great food, and you can work through a good chunk of the menu without committing to a full dinner price. Whatever dish you try, the quality holds up.

They're closed on Mondays. Every other day they open around 11:30am or noon. If you've been sleeping on Indian food in this area, this is the place to fix that.

blurb:
Hamp & Harry's is one of those spots on Roswell Street that just feels right the second you walk in. Good energy, friendly staff, and the kind of place that works for a casual lunch or a Friday night out near the Square. My wife and I have done both and haven't had a bad time yet.

If you go for brunch, get the fried chicken biscuit. I'm talking hot, fluffy, and big enough that you might not finish it in one sitting. That's not a complaint. The salad dressing people keep mentioning in reviews is legitimately worth ordering the side salad.

Just heads up: they're closed on Mondays. Tuesday through Friday they open at 11, and weekends they start at 10, which makes it a solid brunch option if you want to beat the Square crowds.

blurb:
Marietta Fish Market is the kind of place you take family from out of town when you want to actually impress them without driving to Buckhead. The ocean-themed interior is dramatic in the best way, and the portions are not messing around. This place is built for a group.

Seafood is the obvious move here, and the portions reviewers keep raving about are real. Come hungry. It's a solid pick for a family dinner or a special occasion where you want something a little more memorable than your usual rotation.

They're closed Mondays, and dinner service starts at 4pm Tuesday through Friday. Saturday and Sunday they open at noon, which makes the weekend a good window if you want to get in before it fills up.
